title: Gauge Flow Matching: Efficient Constrained Generative Modeling over General Convex Set and Beyond
claim: Constrained generation over a hard-to-handle set becomes easy by mapping it bijectively to a simple domain, generating there, and mapping back.
layout: 2x2 commutative-diagram grid, top-to-bottom, with arrows labeled by ODEs and maps
description: A commutative-diagram layout with two rows. The top row, in red, shows standard flow matching (FM). A Gaussian point cloud at left (x0) connects by a horizontal arrow labeled dx_t/dt = v_x to x1. At right, x1 is a pentagon-shaped convex set C holding two red clusters. The bottom row, in blue, shows gauge flow matching (GFM). A uniform point cloud inside a unit circle (z0) connects by an arrow labeled dz_t/dt = v_z to z1. At right, z1 is a unit ball B holding two blue clusters. Vertical arrows between x1 and z1 are labeled Φ^{-1} (down) and Φ (up), the gauge map. Red marks the original domain and blue marks the transformed ball domain. The eye goes first to the colored scatter plots, then follows the arrows.
caption: Gauge flow matching framework.
abstract: Generative models, particularly diffusion and flow-matching approaches, have achieved remarkable success across diverse domains, including image synthesis and robotic planning. However, a fundamental challenge persists: ensuring generated samples strictly satisfy problem-specific constraints — a crucial requirement for physics-informed problems, safety-critical applications, watermark embedding, etc. Existing approaches, such as mirror maps and reflection methods, either have limited applicable constraint sets or introduce significant computational overhead. In this paper, we develop gauge flow matching (GFM), a simple yet efficient framework for constrained generative modeling. Our GFM approach introduces a novel bijective gauge mapping to transform generation over arbitrary compact convex sets into an equivalent process over the unit ball, which allows low-complexity feasibility-ensuring operations such as reflection or projection. The generated samples are then mapped back to the original domain for output. We prove that our GFM framework guarantees strict constraint satisfaction, with low generation complexity and bounded distribution approximation errors. We further extend our GFM framework to two non-convex settings, namely, star-convex and geodesic-convex sets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GFM outperforms existing methods in both generation speed and quality across multiple benchmarks, including synthetic data, time series, and image generation.
